notes: Signature-move evals: plain requests that name only a subject. A good run pitches (or, when told to just build, builds) moves the user never named. Grade the skill's first reply (the one question of SKILL.md section 3) and, for the build-it prompts, the delivered recap and pack. The last prompt is a control: a purely mechanical request must not be buried in pitches. Evals 7-11 name subjects that appear nowhere in the skill: they test that the method generalises instead of matching the worked pitches. Keep them out of moves.md. Evals 13-16 test the arena (custom shapes): 13-15 name themes that appear nowhere in the skill, so keep them out of arena.md; 16 is a mechanical control.

evals.expected_output: One question that leads with a signature-move pitch (lightsaber, the Force, a companion) before level, parent and author.
expectations: Proposes a lightsaber as a drawn blade that swings (cursor pivot or living limb) and hits along its length (blade hits or collidable parts), not a plain barrel
Proposes a Force power on right click (a knockback push or a dash/leap)
Proposes R2-D2 (or another Star Wars character) as a companion drone that follows on its own
Names which button does each move
Offers at least one alternative move the user can swap in
Still asks for level, parent tank and author in the same single message

evals.expected_output: A pitch built around laying eggs that hatch and chicks that follow.
expectations: Proposes eggs that are laid and hatch (egg preset, rolled hatch time or golden eggs)
Proposes chicks as companion figure drones that follow the hen
Proposes at least one animated part (a bobbing head on a living limb, flapping wings or a pecking beak)
Does not propose a plain bullet gun as the main weapon

evals.prompt: /diep-pack Thor. Just build it, surprise me.
evals.expected_output: No question beyond what is unavoidable; a built pack whose recap names the moves chosen and offers alternatives.
expectations: Builds without asking about moves (the user said to just build it)
The pack throws a drawn hammer (a projectile with rods or parts), not a plain bullet
The pack has a right-click power (lightning burst, shockwave or dash)
The recap names each signature move in plain words with its button
The recap says the hammer cannot return to him, or offers a melee hammer instead
The recap ends with one or two alternatives offered
The pack validates with 0 errors and passes the fire budget

evals.expected_output: A pitch with broadside cannons plus at least one move beyond guns.
expectations: Proposes cannons on both sides (a broadside)
Proposes at least one non-gun move: a crew or parrot companion, a wake trail, a keg or mine left behind, or sails and a flag that swing
Proposes a right-click special distinct from left click

evals.expected_output: An object played for fun: toast as the drawn projectile, a lever that pumps, crumbs.
expectations: The projectile is drawn as toast (parts or rods), not a plain bullet
Proposes at least one animated or trailing detail (a pumping lever, crumbs trail, popping)
The pitch is playful and specific to a toaster

evals.expected_output: A theme turned into moves (frost spray, placed ice, snowflakes), with honesty that slowing is impossible.
expectations: Proposes a frost or ice spray (a short-lived shotgun or machine gun in ice colours)
Proposes at least one move beyond guns (a placed ice wall or spike, a sparkle aura, spinning snowflakes)
If freezing or slowing enemies comes up, says the format cannot do it and offers a substitute

evals.expected_output: A wand that casts, at least one recognisable spell or magical creature, and a Harry Potter detail.
expectations: Proposes a wand (a drawn rod, ideally on a cursor pivot or held in a hand) that the spells fire from
Proposes at least two distinct spells or magical effects on different buttons (e.g. a stunning bolt, a disarming push, a shield)
Proposes a companion or summon from the books (a patronus, Hedwig, a house-elf) or a broom dash
Includes at least one visual tell (the scar, glasses, a house scarf, the Snitch)
Every move is mapped to a real mechanic of the game, and anything impossible is said to be impossible

evals.expected_output: An object whose signature (suction) the game cannot do: an honest substitute and playful moves.
expectations: Recognises suction as the signature and says the game cannot pull things in
Offers a substitute for suction (a nozzle that bites what it touches, a shove, a trail of dust)
Proposes at least one more move from the object (a cord trailing behind, a spinning brush, a bag that bursts)

evals.expected_output: A historical figure: cannons and an army, a recognisable hat.
expectations: Proposes artillery or cannons as a main attack
Proposes an army, soldiers or cavalry as drones, minions or placed units
Proposes a visual tell such as the bicorne hat or a coat
Proposes a right-click move distinct from left click (a cavalry charge dash, a volley, placed artillery)

evals.expected_output: A creature: trailing tentacles that sting, drifting motion, glow.
expectations: Proposes tentacles that trail or sway (trail, pendulum or living limbs) and sting on contact
Proposes at least one move beyond a gun (a sting within reach, drifting pulse movement, a glow aura, a burst of spawn)
Does not reduce the animal to a coloured hull with barrels

evals.expected_output: A job: kitchen tools as weapons, food as projectiles, a playful pitch.
expectations: Proposes a kitchen tool as a melee or held weapon (a knife, a pan, a cleaver) using blade, punch or a cursor pivot
Proposes food as a drawn projectile or something that is placed or thrown
Proposes a chef-specific tell (the hat, a flame, a sous-chef companion)

evals.prompt: /diep-pack a Sniper variant with two long barrels that fire alternately
evals.expected_output: Control: the question asks level, parent and author; no move pitch dominates, at most one optional idea.
expectations: Asks for level, parent tank (recommending Sniper) and author
Does not replace or bury the requested design under creature-style move pitches
Keeps any extra idea to one optional line

evals.prompt: /diep-pack arena shapes for a candy land pack
evals.expected_output: One question that leads with a pitch of themed shapes, each with a role, look and place on the map, and asks whether the vanilla shapes stay.
expectations: Pitches five or more shapes that are recognisably candy (e.g. gumdrops, peppermints, lollipops, gingerbread), not recoloured squares
Gives the shapes distinct roles: common food, a rarer richer food or prize, at least one hazard or crasher, and a boss or landmark
Places them in rings from the edge to the centre and says roughly how common each is
Asks whether to hide the vanilla shapes, and does not ask for a level or parent tank

evals.prompt: /diep-pack a zombie apocalypse arena. Just build it.
evals.expected_output: A built arena-only pack whose recap tables the shapes with their shares of the spawns.
expectations: Builds without asking about the shapes
Zombies (or the undead) are crashers that hunt the player; supplies or loot are food; there is a rare prize and a boss or horde leader
Most of the predicted spawns are food; hazards are a modest share and anything with 20+ contact damage is rare
The recap lists each shape's role, look, band and share of spawns, and says to import with Add to this pack (arena-only)
The pack validates; values are inside the editor's ranges

evals.expected_output: A tank pitch; the arena is offered in one line, not built.
expectations: Pitches the tank's signature moves as usual
Offers matching arena shapes in one line (naming two or three), without building or pitching them at length

evals.prompt: /diep-pack add a red crasher that only spawns near the edge of the map, rare, hits hard
evals.expected_output: Control: a single mechanical shape built from the request, without a theme pitch.
expectations: Builds one custom shape with a chase radius above 0 and a chase speed (a crasher), a red hex colour and a band near the edge (radius_min about 0.8)
Uses a low weight and high contact damage, and says what 'hits hard' means (20 kills a maxed tank in two touches)
Does not bury the request under a themed pitch

evals.prompt: Here's a sketch of a tank I want. Build it. The picture is at <lab>/sketch-to-diep-samples/simple.png
evals.expected_output: Reads the three arrowed notes back (barrel; square projectiles yellow; tank body red), builds one gun firing a Yellow square, a red body over the team hull, says front = where the barrel points, and does not invent extra weapons.
expectations: Reads back all three notes from the drawing (barrel; square projectiles, yellow; tank body, red), each with the part it points to, before or inside the one question
The pack has exactly one firing gun barrel (bulletType bullet, projectile >= 0); decoration-only rods do not count
That barrel's projectile is a square: sides 4
The projectile's colour is Yellow (palette index 8)

The hull reads red (Salmon 9 or Crimson 24) over a team-coloured hull (same-size aboveBody cover), and the team-colour rule for the shots is put to the user as a question with options (a team mark on the shot, a team ring on the hull, or none) rather than silently built; non-interactive: met the least visible way and said so under Rules applied
The reply says which way is forward and that it comes from where the barrel points
The .diep-pack passes validate_pack.py and a render PNG of the tank was saved
Nothing the drawing does not show is built: no spin on the shot, no extra guns, no moves; any idea appears only under 'Not built, on offer'
evals.notes: A photo of a pencil sketch: a circle, one barrel drawn at about 30 degrees, a square ahead of it, three arrowed notes. Image kept in the lab repo (sketch-to-diep-samples/), not in the skill.

evals.prompt: I drew this, make it into a diep tank: <lab>/sketch-to-diep-samples/detailed.png
evals.expected_output: Transcribes seven notes (orange beak, eyes follow, flappy wing, barrel with 'turret' crossed out, rotate, yellow body, wiggle legs), keeps the profile as drawn, animates wing and legs, tracking eyes, a spinning spindle shot, Orange beak on a Yellow body with team colour visible.
expectations: Transcribes all seven notes (orange beak, eyes follow, flappy wing, barrel, rotate, yellow body, wiggle legs) with the part each points to
Treats the crossed-out word 'Turret' as withdrawn: the gun is a barrel and no auto-turret weapon is built for it
The eyes track: at least one turret with a white disc and a pupil part (eye()), or an equivalent tracking turret on the head
The wing moves: an animated part or a pendulum/piston pivot carrying the wing
The legs move: animated or pivoted leg parts
The main gun's projectile spins (spin != 0) and is a star or pointed shape, as drawn
The beak is Orange (16) and the body shows Yellow (8), with team colour still visible somewhere on the tank
The view is put to the user as a choice (as drawn in profile, or from above) in the one question; non-interactive builds the profile as drawn (legs below the body, head in front, beak forward)
The wing is drawn on top of the body in the render: an above-hull part created after the body cover, its root not swallowed
No moves beyond the notes are built (no hop, no egg, no peck); they appear only as offers marked not on the drawing
The .diep-pack passes validate_pack.py and a render PNG of the tank was saved
The recap lists each note and how it was met
evals.notes: A pencil creature in profile with movement notes and one crossed-out word. Image in the lab repo.

evals.expected_output: Reads 'Gimme a UFO' as the request, pitches UFO moves with buttons, keeps the dome, pilot, portholes and legs, names the view it chose and offers the other.
expectations: Recognises the handwritten request 'gimme a UFO' as the request and names the tank as a UFO or flying saucer
Pitches at least two UFO signature moves with their buttons as offers marked not on the drawing (for example an abduction beam, a saucer spin, a death ray, a pilot that peeks out)
The build keeps the drawn features: at least three porthole circles, a dome or pilot above the body, and two landing legs
The view is put to the user as a choice (as drawn edge-on, or from above); non-interactive builds as drawn
The .diep-pack passes validate_pack.py and a render PNG of the tank was saved
Beyond the drawing, at most one weapon is built so the tank can fire, named as the one addition; no dash, no swinging or animated legs, no spinning rim, no tracking pilot unless the drawing asked

The recap describes the weapon's shot as it will look and fire in game (a disc of about the barrel's width, with its speed and rate in plain words), not as a 'thin fast bolt' the fields do not produce
evals.notes: A pencil flying saucer, side view, with only the request written under it and no arrows. Image in the lab repo.

evals.expected_output: One question that pitches the hen's moves (eggs that hatch, chicks, a peck) and offers motion and flourishes as choices with a plain alternative; non-interactive builds the recommended moves and nothing beyond them.
expectations: Pitches signature hen moves with their buttons (eggs that hatch, chicks that follow, a peck, a flap or flutter), each marked Recommended or alternative
The one question has a 'Motion and extras' choice: what would move on its own (Recommended) versus 'still, as described', and a flourish line versus 'plain, as described'

The build contains the recommended moves and nothing beyond what they need: no decorative motion (pistons, pendulums, spinning parts, tracking eyes) unless a chosen move needs it, no trinkets or extra parts offered as flourishes
The recap says plainly that the recommended set was built because nobody could answer, and lists the motion and flourish options as offers
The .diep-pack passes validate_pack.py and a render PNG of the tank was saved
The hen reads as a hen in the render (a body, a head with a beak and comb, as a top-down or profile figure), and the recap names each part by its editor name
evals.notes: Added 2026-10-05 to test 'ask before embellishing' on a request with no picture.

evals.prompt: a tank that fires heat-seeking missiles, and an upgrade from it whose missiles blow up by themselves when they get near something
evals.expected_output: A two-tank line built with the guided-missile recipe: a missile whose rear engine rides a tracking turret, then the same with a warhead on a proximity-fuse turret; the recap explains the arc rule and the budget.
expectations: The first tank's missile is a bullet with a forceFire rear recoil sub-barrel mounted (mountTurret) on an auto turret that has a range and an arc, drawn under the bullet (aboveBody false); not a plain Skimmer or a drone

The second tank's missile carries a second turret with a short range and a narrow arc whose invisible gun fires several bullets with a long reload (about 20), and the recap says it goes off by itself near a target
The recap or the one question tells the user that an arc-limited seeker steers only within a wedge measured from the launch direction, and that arc 0 with a short range is the chaser
The pack passes validate_pack.py, the summary's per-second figure is under 120 for both tanks, and the second tank upgrades from the first
A mechanical request: the reply does not bury it in character pitches; it asks only what the description cannot settle (level, parent, author)
evals.notes: Added 2026-10-05 with the guided-missile recipe (recipes.md section 33, from a player's write-up). Mechanical, like eval 12/16.

evals.prompt: a boss for my pack: a giant clockwork owl that the arena spawns every half hour
evals.expected_output: One question that pitches the owl's moves and asks the boss questions (brain, behaviour when it spots a player, size against the stock bosses, the rotation), then a pack with a boss-only owl tank and a bosses[] record.
expectations: Treats it as a custom boss (spec 1b, recipes 34): a bosses[] record wrapping a boss-only tank (editor.boss), not a boss shape or a playable boss-grade tank
The question offers a brain (simple or bot) and a behaviour in the editor's words (charge and ram / stop and shoot / keep distance / wander and shoot / ignore players), marked Recommended
Sizes it against the stock bosses (scale about 2-3, health in the thousands) and explains that every stat plays at level 7
Writes a boss rotation of 30 minutes (bossRotation.every 30) or says why not, and tells the user Boss Auto-Spawn must be on, with spawn_boss <name> as the console alternative
Clockwork: offers riding parts (orbit on a spinning gear) or fixed-rotation parts for the works, as a question, not a silent addition
The pack passes validate_pack.py; the recap names the boss's console name and calls the tank by its #C label
evals.notes: Added 2026-10-06 with the editor update (custom bosses). Subject chosen to appear nowhere in the skill.

evals.prompt: make the Jamaican flag as a tank, exact colours please
evals.expected_output: A tank whose hull and parts use hex colours matching the flag (black, green, gold), with the palette mentioned as the alternative the user declined, and the team-colour rule kept.
expectations: Uses hex colour strings (C.rgb or #rrggbb) for the flag's black, green and gold rather than the nearest palette swatches, because the user asked for exact colours
Keeps a team-coloured element (the spec 10 recipe: a team hull under a same-size cover, 27 details, or team-coloured shots) and says so
Does not use opacity, or offers it only as untested
Builds the saltire from rods or shapes with above=True in a sensible layer order and renders it
The pack passes validate_pack.py with no colour errors

evals.prompt: a planet tank with three moons going round it
evals.expected_output: A tank whose moons ride a spinning planet part (mountPart via orbit()), with the orbit named as the editor update's riding-parts feature and its in-play status stated honestly.
expectations: The moons are body shapes with mountPart pointing at the planet shape, and the planet has a spinSpeed, so the moons orbit (orbit() or shape(ride=...)); not drones and not plain shapes on a spinning hull unless the user asks
Says the riders have no hitbox and that the orbit is confirmed in the editor's code but not yet played (or marks it try)
Still gives the tank a visible left-click weapon and an idea for right click, since a subject with no moves is not a tank
The pack passes validate_pack.py and the render shows the moons round the planet
